subject: Hosted API — Residency, retention & purge obligations (customer Q&A)
messages:

Cc: Olivia Park <olivia@mediq.com>

Subject: Short residency/retention Qs for our security review

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of our security review we have a short set of targeted questions around data residency, retention, and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. We're working to finalize vendor approvals next week and would appreciate concise answers we can reference in the RFI.

Could you confirm: 1) Where customer request payloads and derived tokens are stored (region), 2) Default retention windows for request/response logs and KV/prefix caches, 3) Whether we can request immediate deletion for a tenant and what the operational timeline looks like, 4) Are backups/replicas stored cross-region by default?

If possible, please include any SLA or ticketing path we should expect for deletion requests and any artifacts you provide as proof (audit logs, purge attestations).

Best,
Nadia
Security Analyst, Nimbus Health

Attachment: Nimbus_Security_RFI_itemized.pdf (reference only)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Short residency/retention Qs for our security review

Hi Nadia — thanks for sending these over. Below are concise answers; attaching a short FAQ and a high-level dataflow diagram for reference. If you want, we can convert this into a short SOC-friendly attestation.

1) Where data is stored (region):
- Hosted API customer request payloads, generated tokens, and ephemeral KV caches are stored in the region you select on sign-up (for Nimbus: US-East by default). We do not shard primary request logs to other geographic regions unless you enable multi-region failover.

2) Default retention windows:
- Request/response logs (raw request body, response): default 30 days for debug logs; customers can request a shorter TTL during onboarding.
- Aggregated telemetry/metrics: retained 13 months for product analytics (not customer-identifiable).
- KV/prefix caches (runtime caches and prefix/KV entries): ephemeral by design — TTLs vary by cache policy but default is 2 hours. Cache entries are not considered persistent datastore records.

3) Tenant data deletion (customer-initiated):
- Self-serve: Customers may submit a deletion request through the Console or API.
- Operational timeline: automated deletion pipeline purges active request logs within 72 hours; residual indices and backups are scheduled for purging within 30 days.
- Proof: We provide a deletion ticket with a timestamp and a downloadable audit line (request id, timestamps, operator id). We can also provide a signed attestation for legal review on request.

4) Backups and replicas:
- Backups are region-scoped by default. Cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration for customers who enable multi-region DR; we do not replicate customer data across regions without explicit customer opt-in.

SLA / ticketing path: For deletion/erasure requests attached to an enterprise contract, our standard SLA is 72 hours for primary purge plus 30 days for residual artifacts. For urgent legal holds / court orders we have an expedited channel via Security & Legal (reach out to security-ops@redwood.ai).

Attachments: Redwood_Residency_Retention_FAQ.pdf; redwood-dataflow-ephemeral-cache.svg

Let me know if Olivia (cc'd) would like a slightly expanded legal attestation.

—Avery
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-07-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — residency, retention & purge (internal)

Quick internal thread to confirm a couple of details Nadia might press on:
- Backups: snapshots are taken daily and retained for the configured retention window (default 30 days). They are encrypted at rest and stored within the same region by default.
- Cache semantics: prefix/KV caches are never written to customer-managed object stores; eviction is automatic and we treat caches as ephemeral runtime state. For deletion requests we also proactively invalidate caches for the tenant to ensure no stale tokens persist.
- Proof artifacts: we can attach the Console audit CSV + an S3 object delete event log (redacted) as evidence.

Ben — can you confirm the exact path for the audit CSV export used in production? Neha — confirm that multi-region replication requires explicit enablement on the account.

Thanks,
Priyom
Platform Reliability (ops)

Hi Nadia / Olivia — following up with the concise answers plus the supplemental artifacts we discussed internally. Inline summary below and attached artifacts for your records.

Summary (short):
- Region: US-East selected for Nimbus by default; no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled.
- Retention: request/response debug logs default 30 days (customizable); runtime caches default 2 hours; aggregated telemetry retained 13 months.
- Deletion: self-serve via Console/API; automated primary purge within 72 hours, residual backup purges within 30 days; we provide ticketed proof and downloadable audit CSVs.
- Backups/replication: region-scoped by default; cross-region is opt-in.

Attachments included: Redwood_Residency_Retention_FAQ.pdf (FAQ + deletion SLA), redwood-dataflow-ephemeral-cache.svg (diagram), sample_audit_export_NB-4821.csv (redacted).
